---
title: "Setup: your free Groq API key"
format: html
---

Every lab in this course calls an LLM through **[Groq](https://groq.com)**, which
serves open Llama models on a free tier that comfortably covers all of it. You
need one key, once, and it takes about two minutes.

## 1. Get the key

1. Go to **<https://console.groq.com/keys>** and sign in (Google or GitHub works).
2. Click **Create API Key**, give it any name.
3. Copy it. It starts with `gsk_`.

You will not be able to see it again after you close the dialog, so paste it
somewhere before moving on.

## 2. Put it in Colab Secrets — not in a cell

In Colab, click the **key icon** in the left sidebar, then **Add new secret**:

- **Name:** `GROQ_API_KEY`
- **Value:** the `gsk_...` key
- Toggle **Notebook access** on

Then every notebook reads it like this:

```python
import os
from google.colab import userdata

os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"] = userdata.get("GROQ_API_KEY")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Never paste the key into a code cell
A key written into a cell gets saved into the notebook, and if you push that
notebook to GitHub the key is public — and stays in git history even after you
delete the line. If that happens, **revoke it immediately** at
<https://console.groq.com/keys> and create a new one.

This is a graded item on the capstone, and it is the most common serious
mistake in submitted projects. See
[Never expose API keys](never_expose_api_keys.qmd).
:::

Running locally instead of Colab? Put it in your environment:

```bash
export GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...        # macOS / Linux
setx GROQ_API_KEY "gsk_..."        # Windows
```

## 3. Install and use

```bash
pip install -qU langchain langchain-groq langgraph
```

```python
from langchain_groq import ChatGroq

llm = ChatGroq(model="llama-3.3-70b-versatile", temperature=0)
print(llm.invoke("Reply with exactly: setup works.").content)
```

If that prints `setup works.` you are ready for every lab.

## Which model to use

| Model | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | **The default for this course.** Tool calling, structured output, routing, agents. |
| `llama-3.1-8b-instant` | Much faster and cheaper on rate limits. Good for simple classification, or when you are iterating. |

Both support tool calling and `with_structured_output`, which is what the agent
lessons depend on. The current list is at
<https://console.groq.com/docs/models>.

::: {.callout-important}
## Groq does not do embeddings
Groq serves **chat completions only** — there is no embeddings endpoint. The
RAG lessons therefore embed with a local, free HuggingFace model:

```python
from langchain_huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbeddings

embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(model_name="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
```

It downloads once and then runs offline on the machine, with no key at all. The
[Embeddings lesson](04_embeddings.ipynb) uses OpenRouter to show a hosted
embeddings API; everywhere else, the local model above is enough.
:::

## Rate limits

The free tier limits requests and tokens per minute. If you see a **429**, you
have two options — both already taught in
[Reliability](13_reliability.qmd):

- add a `RetryPolicy` so transient limits retry themselves, and
- drop to `llama-3.1-8b-instant` while iterating, and switch back to the 70B
  model for your final run.

Current limits: <https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits>.
